summary.one_liner: faf-cli generates AI coding agent context files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules) from a single project.faf file, detected from the repo's actual stack, and scores how complete that context is.
summary.what_it_does: The CLI detects a repository's stack and fills the slots of a typed project.faf file (YAML, IANA-registered as application/vnd.faf+yaml). The `faf export` command then authors AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and .cursorrules from that one source. `faf score` reports AI-readiness as a 0–100% score against 33 slots, with tiers from Trophy (100%) down to Red. Other commands cover `faf git` for a shallow clone of any GitHub repo, `faf check` to validate a .faf file, `faf show` to render it as HTML, `faf diff`/`log` for context changes across git history, and `faf hooks --install` for a pre-commit guard. The README also describes a companion .fafm memory format and a .fafa agent identity format with card-generation commands.
use_cases: keep CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md in sync with the codebase
generate AI agent context files from a repo
score how complete a repo's AI context is
guard against context regression in pre-commit hooks
convert Claude memory into portable .fafm files
share project context with every clone via git
notable: One project.faf file is the single origin for multiple assistant context files
Deterministic score across 33 slots, with Trophy tier as the target
Stack detection fills slots from the repo's real files
Dogfoods itself: CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md are authored from project.faf
Distributed across npm, PyPI and crates.io with an IANA-registered media type
caveats: The README says AGENTS.md in this repo is hand-kept, so `faf export --agents` is not the source for it here
Scoring targets 100% (Trophy) and the README says sub-Trophy states leave gaps; the score is only as good as the slots filled
Several features (cards, memory, skills types) are described as newer editions, so behavior may change between versions
